story: It's a bright, 75-degree Sunday morning in Sumter Oaks, and Gary is tinkering at his workbench at home, tightening a speaker bracket and tidying up a tangle of light strip wiring. Across the way, Donna is penciling a two-hour practice slot with Gary onto the club calendar, cheerfully noting an upcoming ladder match. Meanwhile, Hal is peering through his binoculars along Magnolia Loop, keeping an eye out for early Halloween decorations and counting ornaments, while Rosa wraps up the last dishes and wipes down the long dining table.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Fine-tune the speaker bracket and tidy the light strip wiring, all indoors
Donna (donna club calendar): Pencil in a two-hour practice slot with Gary and note the upcoming ladder match
Hal (hal binoculars): Take another careful look up and down Magnolia Loop for early Halloween decorations and any ornament counts worth noting
Rosa (rosa dining table): Finish clearing the last dishes and wipe down the long table

gary.thought_process: Quiet Sunday morning, nobody around. Last tick I bench-tested the light strips and speaker wiring indoors, which is fine since it's inside the house. The cart stays in the garage until the Architectural Review board signs off (L-01), and I don't want to risk a notice with Hal. The sound system is the part I can keep refining at the bench without breaking any rule, since it's indoors and well before 10 PM. A little tinkering on the speaker mounting bracket keeps me useful and keeps the parade project moving while I wait on the board.

parameters.content: Fine-tune the speaker bracket and tidy the light strip wiring, all indoors

donna.thought_process: It's Sunday morning, I'm home alone, and my last action was checking the pickleball bag for Gary's spare paddle and extra balls. Gary and I have a ladder match coming up and I want us to climb past Pruitt-Kowalski. The club calendar is right here, so I should lock in our next practice slot and keep the club schedule organized. Court reservations max out at 2 hours per party (L-05), so I'll plan within that limit. No one is nearby to talk to, and I shouldn't repeat what I already did with the bag.

parameters.content: Pencil in a two-hour practice slot with Gary and note the upcoming ladder match

hal.thought_process: Sunday morning, quiet Loop, nobody in sight. Last night's dinner at Rosa's went well and my notebook is squared away. Halloween flyer went up, and decorations are welcome all week, so I want to see what's already going up. I was scanning the Loop last tick with the binoculars; one more careful pass from the porch is cheap, and anything over three ornaments or a cart modification still bears noting. Better to keep an eye out than to wait and be surprised.

parameters.content: Take another careful look up and down Magnolia Loop for early Halloween decorations and any ornament counts worth noting

rosa.thought_process: The welcome dinner went beautifully last night, and my last action was clearing off the dishes and wiping down the long table. It's Sunday morning, nobody's around, and I can't speak to anyone. The table is the unfinished business here, and I'd rather finish cleaning now than leave it sitting. Then I can check my shift schedule and see what the week holds. Halloween on the Loop is next Saturday and I'd love to be part of it with Donna, Gary and Hal, but that can wait until I see them.

parameters.content: Finish clearing the last dishes and wipe down the long table

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
